requirement: Atomic multi-item order placement POST /orders decrementing product stock and creating OrderItem records, rolling back all database mutations cleanly when any product has insufficient stock.
skeleton: FastAPI order placement endpoint with multi-item inventory validation and atomic SQLAlchemy transaction rollback.
caption: A FastAPI order service whose order placement is one atomic SQLAlchemy transaction over in-memory SQLite. The schema has three tables under a DeclarativeBase: Product with name, integer stock, and float price; Order with a total_price defaulting to 0.0 and an items relationship; and OrderItem with order_id and product_id foreign keys, quantity, unit_price, and a back-reference to its order. reset_db drops and recreates the schema, and get_db yields one session per request and closes it in finally. pydantic models cover product creation and response, an OrderItemRequest of product_id and quantity, an OrderCreate carrying a list of them, and order item and order responses read from ORM attributes. POST /products answers 201; GET /products/{product_id} and GET /orders/{order_id} raise HTTPException 404 when the row is missing; GET /orders lists every order. POST /orders first rejects an empty item list with HTTPException 400. It then creates an Order and, inside a try block, walks every requested line: a missing product raises HTTPException 404, a quantity greater than the available stock raises HTTPException 400 with detail Insufficient stock, and otherwise the stock is decremented, the line total accumulated, and an OrderItem added at the product's current price. A quantity exactly equal to the remaining stock passes the check. Only after every line succeeds does the handler set total_price, commit once, refresh, and return 201. Any HTTPException, and any other Exception, triggers db.rollback before re-raising, so a failure on the last line leaves every earlier stock value untouched and the session clean for the next request.

rationale.teaches: An atomic multi-row order: validate every line first, commit once, roll back on any failure, and treat exactly-remaining stock as sufficient.
rationale.why: A partial commit leaves inventory inconsistent while every request still returns a sensible status. Checking stock after a deliberately failed order is the only way to see it, and the fixture does exactly that.

candidates.why_wrong: Each line is committed inside the loop, so when a later line fails the earlier stock decrements survive the rollback.
The failed order is never rolled back, so the pending decrements stay in the dirty session and can leak into the next commit.
An order for exactly the remaining stock is rejected as insufficient.
Stock is decremented without being checked, so an order can drive stock negative and still succeed.
The order is only flushed, never committed, so the decrement and the OrderItem rows vanish when the session ends.
